executive_summary: The window closes with the 2026 Met Gala (Monday, May 4), the Costume Institute's highest-visibility annual event, run under the 'Fashion Is Art' dress code tied to its spring exhibition 'Costume Art.' Institutional framing (Metropolitan Museum of Art) and broad editorial/entertainment-press pickup converge tightly on this single dated event, the strongest-corroborated signal of the window. Separately, editorial and retail-facing coverage of spring/summer 2026 street style continues to document an accessories-forward cluster -- oversized silk scarves worn as garments, team jerseys styled outside sport context, plaid/check prints, and midi skirts -- corroborated across editorial, retail, and trade-intelligence sources, though this is season-long documentation rather than an event tied specifically to this seven-day window. A single dated trade item -- WWD's spring 2026 denim runway roundup, published April 27, the window's opening day -- is carried as a lower-confidence, single-source item. Independent criticism (Derek Guy's Die, Workwear Substack) was checked but returned only general newsletter/audience description for this period, not a specific dated claim, and was not logged as a standalone signal.

top_signals.name: Met Gala 2026 'Fashion Is Art' dress code / Costume Institute 'Costume Art' exhibition
top_signals.evidence: Metropolitan Museum of Art press release confirms the Costume Institute's spring 2026 exhibition 'Costume Art' (on view May 10, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027) and the associated benefit gala's dress code, 'Fashion Is Art,' inviting sculptural, draped, sheer/nude-referencing, and museum-statue-evoking dress. The gala itself was held Monday, May 4 (the final day of this window), co-chaired by Beyonce, Nicole Kidman, Venus Williams, and Anna Wintour, with Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez Bezos as honorary chairs/lead sponsors. Vogue hosted the official livestream. NPR, CBS News, and E! Online each ran preview and same-day coverage explaining the theme and cataloguing early red-carpet interpretations (e.g. Emma Chamberlain's Van Gogh-referencing custom Mugler, Sabrina Carpenter's Audrey Hepburn 'Sabrina'-referencing custom Dior).
top_signals.index_note: Origin classification is recorded as 'unclear' rather than forced into an existing category: the signal originates from an institutional exhibition/gala framework (the Costume Institute setting an annual theme), which is not the same as designer-originated, editorial-amplified, retail-adopted, or social-amplified as those terms are used elsewhere in this taxonomy. Treated as a single-window 'flash' event rather than an ongoing style signal -- the theme itself does not carry forward into future weeks the way a garment or aesthetic trend would, though specific red-carpet looks may seed downstream editorial-amplified signals in later reports.
top_signals.human_editor_note: First real (non-thin, non-fictional-date) report produced for this archive. This signal was chosen because it is the most tightly and verifiably dated item found in the window -- an institutional press release plus same-day broadcast/entertainment-press coverage, not a synthesized trend roundup. Confirmed real via WebSearch, not fabricated.

top_signals.name: Spring/summer 2026 accessories-forward street style cluster (oversized silk scarves, team jerseys, plaid/check, midi skirts)
top_signals.evidence: Harper's Bazaar Singapore's spring/summer 2026 street style and runway trend roundups, Who What Wear's Paris street-style-shopping coverage and a dedicated 'tassel scarf' trend piece, and Trendalytics' SS26 street-style-trends insight report independently converge on the same cluster: oversized silk scarves worn as tops, dresses, or bag slings (runway-originated at Hermes, Celine, Miu Miu, Lanvin per Harper's Bazaar and Who What Wear); soccer/team jerseys styled with heels or tailored trousers; plaid/check prints (framed by Harper's Bazaar Singapore as 'school chic with a rebellious twist'); and midi skirts in sheer, suede, or lace across multiple fashion-week cities. Who What Wear's Paris coverage additionally names printed silk scarves, statement belts, and barrel bags as recurring street-style pieces.
top_signals.index_note: This is season-long documentation (spring/summer 2026 runway-to-street adoption), not a claim that the cluster emerged newly within this specific seven-day window -- flagged honestly rather than implying week-specific novelty. Classified 'retail_adopted' because the cited evidence centers on documented street-style/consumer wear rather than the runway origination itself, though runway origin (Hermes/Celine/Miu Miu/Lanvin) is noted in evidence for traceability. trendalytics.co is a B2B trend-forecasting vendor (taxonomy.SOURCE_SECTORS 'trade_intelligence', added run 100) -- included here as one of three corroborating sectors, not the sole source, consistent with that sector's known commercial-incentive noise profile.

top_signals.name: Spring 2026 runway denim: polished washes, '90s-baggy volume, saturated color
top_signals.evidence: WWD's spring 2026 denim-trends roundup, published April 27 (the opening day of this collection window), reports no single dominant 'it' jean across the spring 2026 runways but instead three convergent threads: polished, refined classic-wash denim (MM6 Maison Margiela straight-leg), '90s-influenced voluminous/baggy silhouettes (Stella McCartney's organic-cotton Relaxed Curve jeans), and saturated color (lavender at Chloe, rose-hued denim via an Agolde collaboration, a full rainbow range at Versace).
top_signals.index_note: Single-source item (WWD only found for this specific dated claim); confidence held at 'medium' per derive_confidence() -- one high-reliability (editorial) sector, corroboration_count 1. Not upgraded on the strength of the outlet's reputation alone, consistent with this archive's confidence discipline.

limitations: WebSearch (not direct WebFetch of full article text) was the sole research tool used; findings rest on search-result snippets and synthesized summaries rather than full primary-source article text.

Most spring/summer 2026 street-style and runway-trend coverage found is season-long aggregated content (published across March-May 2026) rather than precisely dated to this seven-day window; only the WWD denim piece (April 27) and the Met Gala coverage (May 4) are tightly dated within the window itself. The street-style cluster signal is explicitly framed as ongoing seasonal documentation, not week-specific novelty.

Independent criticism (dieworkwear.substack.com / Derek Guy) was checked but returned only general newsletter/traffic description for this period, with no specific dated claim substantive enough to log as a standalone signal -- excluded rather than forced.

Four source domains encountered for the first time this run (harpersbazaar.com.sg, eonline.com, cbsnews.com, npr.org) were classified by hand-research rather than via an existing taxonomy.DOMAIN_SECTOR_MAP entry; see docs/agent-logs/real-research-2026-05-04.md for the reasoning. taxonomy.py itself was not edited (out of scope for this task).
